action: ShebaMiles members: change your password (and reuse nowhere else), watch the account for unusual activity, and treat unexpected emails about it as possible phishing.
date_note: Date of the airline's customer notice; the intrusion date was not stated.
exec: A national airline has told frequent-flyer customers their information may have been affected; passenger loyalty data is a ready phishing source.
plain: Ethiopian Airlines told ShebaMiles frequent-flyer members that certain customer information may have been affected. It says there is no evidence financial information was accessed. Addis Fortune reported fewer than 8,000 accounts reached.

sources.name: CIO Africa (relaying Reuters and Addis Fortune)

summary: Ethiopian Airlines notified ShebaMiles members on 18 November of a limited-scope incident, saying customer information might have been affected and there is no evidence financial information was accessed. CIO Africa says the CEO confirmed an investigation to Reuters; Addis Fortune reported fewer than 8,000 accounts reached and suspicious activity detected on 17 November. Data types were not disclosed.
title: Ethiopian Airlines reports ShebaMiles frequent-flyer data incident

validation.note: Airline customer notice reported by Capital Ethiopia and Fidel Post; number affected and data types not disclosed.
